title: Tenant Residency Decision Trace & Compact Compliance Bundle
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Customers and auditors need a compact, machine-verified package that explains why a given tenant's hosted API traffic was routed to particular regions, how long data was retained, and proof artifacts for configuration/controls (routing policy, retention rules, KMS usage). Existing evidence exports are large and verbose, and auditors frequently ask for a concise bundle that supports automated verification.

Goal: Implement a 'Residency Decision Trace' API and a compact compliance bundle builder that can be invoked by the Console (or via API/CLI) to produce a verifiable artifact containing: a human-readable summary, ordered decision trace (policy evaluations + fallback steps), signed configuration snapshots, retention metadata, sample request IDs (redacted), and cryptographic references to keys used. The bundle should be small (<50KB typical for a one-day snapshot of a tenant) and structured for both auditors and downstream ingestion into compliance tooling.

Scope:
- Backend API: /v1/tenants/:tenant_id/residency-bundle (POST) that accepts time window, redaction level, and output format (zip or tar.gz).
- Decision trace: capture stepwise policy evaluation (policy id, matched predicate, input attributes, chosen region, fallback region if any, timestamp, rationale). Store a cryptographic hash for each decision step.
- Retention mapping: include the tenant's effective retention profile at time of bundle (names and expiry rules) and canonical mapping to storage classes.
- Proof artifacts: signed snapshots of tenant routing policy, effective pinset, and the routing engine's region affinity scores for the sampled window. Reference KMS key ARNs and include KMS-wrapped key metadata (not raw keys).
- Console flow: 'Export Compliance Bundle' action in Tenant Settings -> Residency with a confirmation modal describing redaction and retention options. Exports appear in Compliance Exports list with a signed checksum and TTL.
- CLI: redwood residency export --tenant <id> --from <ts> --to <ts> --redaction compact|full --format zip

Acceptance criteria:
1) API returns a signed bundle with the components listed above for a sample tenant and one-day window.
2) Bundle verification script (python) validates signatures and hashes and outputs pass/fail and a short human summary.
3) Console UI provides the export action and shows export status with checksum and download link.
4) Export size for a tenant with normal traffic stays under 100KB; tests for larger customers included.

Design trade-offs and decisions:
- We will not include raw request payloads by default. Instead we include request IDs and redacted headers; full payloads require explicit customer opt-in and will be gated behind a legal/compliance workflow.
- To keep bundles compact, we will store only the policy diffs (what changed) between the start and end of the window, plus a canonical snapshot at the point of export.
- Signature scheme: Use existing KMS signing service to avoid building new crypto. The bundle includes the signing key ID, signature, and certificate chain URL.

Implementation notes (backend):
- New lightweight service residency-bundler runs as a job on Dedicated/Hosted control plane. It queries the routing decision store (time-series) and policy DB, computes diffs, generates manifest.json and signs it via KMS.
- The bundler must be able to operate in-station (region) to avoid cross-region retrieval of sensitive logs; it will call into our internal proxy to retrieve hashes only.
- Add index entries to Compliance Exports (Console) with metadata: size, checksum, created_by, redaction_level, expiry_ts.

Security & privacy considerations:
- Marked for mandatory security_review_required. Redaction levels determine whether IPs or request bodies are included. Default is 'compact' which strips IPs and payloads.
- Ensure export TTL is enforced (auto-delete) and access is RBAC-controlled. Only users with 'compliance:export' role can invoke or download.

Open questions:
- Should we include an opaque audit token that lets auditors fetch on-demand raw payloads under an MSA with the customer? (suggested: out-of-scope for initial iteration)
- How to represent policy predicates that are time-window sensitive? Proposed: add predicate_ttl and evaluation_context snapshot.

Deliverables:
- API spec and OpenAPI fragment in the ticket.
- Console UI mockups and copy.
- bundler service implementation + unit/integration tests.
- verification script and CI job for sample tenants.

Related artifacts: design doc: https://docs.redwood.ai/confluence/Residency/compact-bundle-v1, mockups: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/Residency-Export-Mocks, sample PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/7622
